subject: Paloma-lite-7b onboarding: compatibility checks + pin request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Paloma-lite-7b intake + pin ask (initial intake)

Hey team,

Paloma Labs just handed over the paloma-lite-7b artifacts and asked for an onboarding window. They flagged two items that will matter for us in production:

- Tokenizer differences vs our standard BPE variant (they have a small merged-vocab).
- New weight layout which may impact our fused-kernel paths (they included an int8 quantized variant).

They've requested we pin the current model sha for 30 days after initial rollout to avoid accidental auto-roll of a patched checkpoint. Maria (Paloma) suggested a provisional version label: paloma-lite-7b:v2028-07-01.

Can we confirm the following by EOD?
1) What tests do runtime/infra need to sign off on the pin (tokenizer parity, kv-cache correctness, perf numbers)?
2) Any known blockers for our non-fp16 fused kernels if we accept their int8 artifact?
3) Recommended canary percentage and a safe rollout window (hours/days) for a new 7B variant.

Attached: paloma_compat_checklist.xlsx, sample_prompts_and_outputs.jsonl

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@paloma.ai>
Date: 2028-07-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Paloma-lite-7b intake + pin ask

Thanks for the heads-up, Soojin. Short answers up front:

- Runtime needs tokenizer parity (exact byte-level tokenization on our official prompt sets), KV-cache replay tests on long-conversation traces, and a 95th-percentile latency check for our standard 512-token inference profile.
- Int8 may skip some of our optimized FP16 kernels; Dev, can you enumerate which paths would fall back and estimate latency impact?
- For a 7B, a 5% -> 25% -> 100% staged canary over 48 hours is our normal baseline; we can compress to 24h if telemetry looks clean.

Requested ask: if Paloma wants the 30-day pin, we'll need a JIRA (INF-5387) and a pinned version in the model registry with a human owner and an auto-expiry reminder. Laura — can you start the registry entry and assign the owner?

I'll put the runtime test matrix into INF-5387 this morning.

-Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-08T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Paloma-lite-7b intake + pin ask

Quick technical note after an initial artifact scan:

- Tokenizer: Paloma's merged-vocab increases single-token coverage and shifts some split points; several of our eval prompts produce different token counts. We'll need to either adopt their tokenizer or add a mapping layer at tokenization time. Mapping adds runtime overhead (roughly +1.5ms per request at 512 tokens in our microbench).

- KV-cache: Their attention key ordering matches standard layout, but they use a different past-kv dtype on the quantized build. We'll validate with a replay test — I flagged a long-chat trace in the Drive folder.

- Kernels: If we use the int8 artifact, metric-wise I expect fallback to our reference interpreter for ~12% of attention ops that currently use fused CUDA kernels on Ampere/Turing. On typical 7B traffic that could yield a 10–18% p95 latency increase unless we compile a new kernel or push them an fp16 build.

Proposed short-term plan:
1) Accept paloma-lite-7b:v2028-07-01 into staging with pin.
2) Run tokenizer parity + KV replay + perf smoke in staging (24–36h).
3) If perf regressions >10% p95, hold pin and request an fp16 weights drop from Paloma or schedule a targeted kernel pass.

I'll run the perf smoke this afternoon and post results to INF-5387.

-Dev

--
Dev Patel

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Paloma-lite-7b intake + pin ask (action items)

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps (agree/modify):

- Jordan: create INF-5387 and schedule pin request in model registry; set auto-expiry reminder for 2028-08-01.
- Laura: create the model registry entry and assign short-term owner.
- Dev: run tokenizer parity, KV replay, and perf smoke in staging today; post results to INF-5387. If p95 regress >10% we pause and request fp16 weights from Paloma.
- Karthik: please confirm canary cadence and monitoring hooks (cost/latency/error budgets). I propose 5%->25%->100% over 48h with an automated rollback if p95 or error rate breaches thresholds.

Maria — thanks for the artifacts. If Paloma can provide an fp16 weights tarball this week it will reduce risk; otherwise we'll proceed with the plan above but may need a short hold.

I'll mark this thread as the intake record in the Drive folder and link INF-5387.

Thanks,
Soojin
